gap: No result ChatGPT got states that on the UGREEN Nexode 100W 4-port charger the USB-A port works only alongside C1 or C2 (not C3), that plugging in a third device cuts the laptop port from 65 W to 45 W, and that its PPS tops out at 25 W, so a Galaxy S24/S25 Ultra cannot get Samsung's 45 W Super Fast Charging 2.0 from it.
standout_why: I opened publicasta.com (cited), itechguides.com 100W multiport (cited) and androidauthority.com best USB-C chargers (cited). Publicasta only says in general terms that a 100 W charger 'might give the laptop 65 W' and that you need 100 W/240 W e-marked cables. Itechguides lists power splits for other UGREEN SKUs (X757, 90928) and gives no split for the US 4-port, and it has no port exclusion. Android Authority ticks PPS boxes and gives Anker Prime 100W splits but nothing for the Nexode 100W 4-port's ports, and it never ties a charger's 25 W PPS cap to Samsung's 45 W mode. None says which port the laptop, phone, power bank and watch should each use. wired.com and travelandleisure.com (both cited) blocked fetching, so I could not check them. They are adapter round-ups, which makes charger port rules unlikely there. That is why this scores 2 and not 3. The finding sets the port plan for this kit but would not change which products go in it.
kit_items: Wall charger: UGREEN Nexode 100W 4-Port (3× USB-C + USB-A). C1 or C2 gives up to 100 W at 20 V/5 A for a laptop. Input is 100–240 V, so overseas only a plug adapter is needed, not a voltage converter. Port plan: laptop on C1 (65 W with a second device), phone on C2 (30 W), earbuds or watch on C3. Never use C3 and USB-A as a pair.

Power bank: UGREEN Nexode 20,000 mAh 100W (72 Wh, below the 100 Wh airline line). Its USB-C input takes up to 20 V/3.25 A (65 W), which matches the charger's 65 W C1 slot when a phone sits on C2, so the bank recharges at full rate next to the phone. Only its C1 output reaches 20 V/5 A, so the laptop goes on C1 of the bank. C2 stops at 12 V/2.5 A (30 W).
Cables: two UGREEN 100 W USB-C to USB-C cables (included in the power bank bundle). A 20 V/5 A port needs a 5 A cable to give 100 W. A 5 A cable is also what Samsung asks for in its 45 W mode.

findings.product: UGREEN Nexode 100W 4-Port Charger + Samsung Galaxy S24/S25 Ultra
findings.label: Samsung charging rate
findings.value: 25 W (Super Fast Charging), not 45 W (Super Fast Charging 2.0)
findings.source_title: Samsung US – Galaxy device is not fast charging
findings.note: Samsung says 2.0 needs 'a 45W or 60W USB-C adapter and a 5A-rated USB-C cable'. Samsung's 45 W adapter page (https://www.samsung.com/ca/mobile-accessories/45w-power-adapter-black-ep-t4511xbegca/, read 2026-11-11) lists PPS 5.0–20.0 V and names S22+/Ultra through S25 Ultra as 2.0 models. UGREEN lists this charger's PPS as 25 W. The 25 W ceiling is my inference from these documents and has not been measured. James Smythe charged an S24 Ultra but gave no wattage.

findings.label: Input / outputs / energy
findings.value: Input USB-C up to 20 V/3.25 A (65 W); C1 out up to 20 V/5 A (100 W, PPS); C2 out up to 12 V/2.5 A (30 W); USB-A out up to 22.5 W; 72 Wh
findings.source_title: (Bundle) 100W 20000mAh Power Bank + 3.3FT 100W USB-C Cable 2 Pack – UGREEN US
findings.note: UGREEN spec block. 72 Wh is below the 100 Wh carry-on limit cited by publicasta. Only C1 reaches 20 V, so a laptop must use C1. A 65 W input means the charger's 65 W C1 slot (with a phone on C2) recharges it at full rate. The standalone bank page (https://us.ugreen.com/products/ugreen-100w-20000mah-power-bank) is $79.99 and shows the same spec.
